corrected_issues: Export originally could produce out-of-bound physics state that import rejected. Export now rejects unsupported state, and inclusive position/180-degree yaw boundaries are tested.
Restoration originally would execute new-game Initialize. Explicit restore construction skips it; actual initialization-marker rejection verifies this on both gameplay backends.

The first CoreCLR qualification used a late native environment change that the hosted runtime did not observe. A test-owned file marker configured before runtime startup replaced that harness assumption.
limitations: The host supplies and is responsible for verifying the full frozen content digest and original definition.
No automatic schema migration or dev/shipping-backend save interchange; exact module image/type/schema required.
Solver/contact caches, sleep timers, DSP buffers and presentation state are reconstructed, not persisted; no general bit-identical physics trajectory claim.
Caller-owned executable configuration can run trusted constructors/statics; external effects are outside the staged-world transaction.
Existing immutable entity set only; general component graphs, spawn/despawn, inventories, streamed regions and environmental subsystems are not qualified.
JSON capture is synchronous and allocates; no production pause/memory/throughput budget qualified.
Test-only file exchange is not a durable write protocol, power-loss qualification or recovery/slot system.
No GUI change or graphics qualification in this milestone; the existing verified editor package remains active.
